findings.title: Three incompatible external-action vocabularies and conflicting defaults

evidence.description: EXTERNAL_ACTIONS.md used AUTO_ALLOWED/ASSISTED/APPROVAL_REQUIRED/HIGH_RISK_APPROVAL; SECURITY.md listed READ/DRAFT/APPROVE/PUBLISH/DEPLOY/BILLING/DESTRUCTIVE (no account creation); permissions.json listed 8 lowercase classes.
manifest.json externalActionDefault = approval_required while permissions.json default = deny_external_write.

findings.impact: Agents and future code could authorize account creation or publishing under the wrong tier.
findings.remediation: Single scope vocabulary mapped to risk tiers T0-T3 (ADR-015); SECURITY.md references it; machine files aligned and checked.

verification.method: machine state test: permissions.json scopes equal common scope enum; defaults agree; EXTERNAL_ACTIONS.md lists every scope

findings.title: Incomplete authority chain

evidence.description: Hierarchy omitted RESEARCH_POLICY.md, EXTERNAL_ACTIONS.md, SCHEMAS.md, UX.md, DATA_MODEL.md and every Everything-layer file (PREMIUM_EXPERIENCE_OS.md, AI_RUNTIME_OS.md, EVERYTHING_OS.md, review gates, tooling/, media/, automation/, operations/, governance/, capabilities/); manifest.json ranked first but contains no rules.

findings.impact: Conflicts between canonical requirement files had no defined resolution.
findings.remediation: Complete hierarchy in AGENTS.md with strongest-rule principle; machine files declared mirrors checked by npm run check.

findings.title: Evidence states undefined

evidence.description: CONFIRMED vs OBSERVED vs INFERRED had no definitions; research fact-vs-estimate, evidence state and confidence were conflated.

findings.impact: Research could be labelled CONFIRMED without human verification.
findings.remediation: Definitions in AGENTS.md; three independent axes in the research contract; automated research capped at OBSERVED; CONFIRMED requires human review (schema-enforced).

verification.method: machine state test: AGENTS.md defines every evidence state; research-claim mutation rejects CONFIRMED without human review

findings.title: Gate results lack FAIL and machine-readable evidence

evidence.description: Result vocabulary was PASS | BLOCKED | NOT_APPLICABLE; no place to record criteria evidence.

findings.impact: An evaluated-but-failed gate could only be recorded as BLOCKED; PASS could be asserted narratively.
findings.remediation: FAIL added; GateResult schema requires evidence for PASS criteria; results stored in gates/results/.

verification.method: gate-result mutations reject PASS with FAIL criterion, PASS without evidence, BLOCKED without blockers

findings.title: MVP pipeline and journey include P1 features

evidence.description: ARCHITECTURE.md ended the MVP pipeline with 'Preview / ZIP / Git' and UX.md listed 'connect repository' and 'project health' while PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md places GitHub and health scoring in P1.

findings.impact: Scope creep into MVP.
findings.remediation: Git connection and health scoring marked P1 in both files.

findings.title: Schema requirements incomplete and non-machine-readable

evidence.description: SCHEMAS.md prose covered 5 types; ModuleDefinition, Recommendation, GateResult, Capability, Tool/Model provider, MediaAsset, ConsentRecord, AutomationDefinition and Handoff were missing; ProjectProfile lacked distribution model, assumptions, mode and business operations required elsewhere.

findings.impact: No deterministic contract for the compiler and engines.
findings.remediation: 15 versioned JSON Schemas with fixtures and negative mutation tests.

verification.method: all 17 required schema types compile with valid fixtures and 48 rejected mutations

findings.title: Missing boundary for second-order prompt injection and approval spoofing

evidence.description: Generated Project OS files are consumed by coding agents as instructions; research and user text flowing into them unfenced would become executable instructions. No rule prevented 'already approved' text in imported content from counting as approval.

findings.impact: Downstream coding agents could be steered by attacker-controlled research content; approvals could be spoofed.
findings.remediation: Untrusted text rendered only in labelled data blocks and never in rule sections (validated at compile); approvals human-only and bound to payload hash.

findings.title: Canonical requirements absent from PRD P0

evidence.description: Premium UX, AI cost harness (declared canonical by prompts/CLAUDE_CYCLE0_ADDENDUM.md) and business-goal intake were not in PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md; APPLY_THIS_UPDATE.md recommended adding references.

findings.impact: Milestones could omit required quality and cost controls.
findings.remediation: P0 sections added, marked for ratification; scope classification in plan/SCOPE.md.

findings.title: Inconsistent module lists across documents

evidence.description: PRD examples (local marketplace, internal tool), bootstrap list (growth, BI, operations) and Everything layer domains differed with no registry.

findings.impact: Unclear which modules exist.
findings.remediation: modules/registry.json (22 modules) covers all lists; marketplace and internal tool are product types handled by web-saas.

findings.title: Missing lifecycle/state rules and data-rights requirements

evidence.description: Inventory statuses INITIALIZED/FUTURE were undefined; state.json duplicated CURRENT_STATE.md with no precedence; handoffs/ did not exist; no requirement for project deletion/export or AI data disclosure.

findings.impact: State drift and unverifiable cycle closure; privacy expectations undefined.
findings.remediation: Status vocabularies in AGENTS.md; state.json declared a checked mirror; handoffs/ created with schema; data-rights P0 requirements added (ratify).

findings.title: Module selection inputs included stack

evidence.description: modules.json selectionInputs listed 'stack' while stack recommendation needs selected modules.

findings.impact: Potential circular dependency in the pipeline.
findings.remediation: Selection consumes profile facts only; stack recommendation consumes selected modules.

findings.title: Two ADR locations

evidence.description: DECISIONS.md held ADRs while the Cycle 0 prompt requires architecture/decisions/.

findings.impact: Decisions could diverge.
findings.remediation: DECISIONS.md is the index with short records; long ADRs in architecture/decisions/.

findings.title: 301 capability files are identical boilerplate with no metadata

evidence.description: Hashing file bodies after the title line showed every capability stub shares one template; nothing recorded phase, dependencies, consent, scopes or cost.

findings.impact: Selective activation and MVP scope discipline impossible to enforce.
findings.remediation: Generated capabilities/registry.json with explicit, checked classification; stubs marked STUB with no independent authority.

verification.method: capability registry test: ids equal taxonomy, one doc each, phases and dependencies consistent

findings.title: Same-named files with different subjects

evidence.description: Case-insensitive name collisions with capabilities/ai/{MODEL_ROUTING,TOKEN_HARNESS,CLAUDE_CODE}.md, capabilities/marketing/SOCIALS.md, capabilities/recovery/TECH_DEBT.md, capabilities/docs/README.md; overlapping topics capabilities/marketing/COMPETITORS.md and capabilities/design/MOTION.md.

findings.impact: Agents may read the stub instead of the canonical contract.
findings.remediation: Kept separate (1stStep OS runtime vs generated-project capability); AGENTS.md terminology and hierarchy state stubs carry no authority.

findings.title: RETENTION capability name ambiguous

evidence.description: Both files had byte-identical bodies titled 'Retention' although one means user retention and the other data retention.

findings.impact: Wrong guidance generated for privacy retention.
findings.remediation: Retitled 'User Retention' and 'Data Retention'.

findings.title: Nested AGENTS.md stub could act as agent instructions

evidence.description: capabilities/ai/AGENTS.md existed alongside the root AGENTS.md.
Some coding agents load AGENTS.md files from nested directories as scoped instructions.

findings.impact: A boilerplate stub could override or dilute canonical authority for work under capabilities/.
findings.remediation: Renamed to capabilities/ai/AI_AGENTS.md; AGENTS.md forbids nested AGENTS.md; check enforces; compiler validation forbids them in bundles.

verification.method: test: only the root AGENTS.md exists

findings.title: Three divergent premium UI review lists

evidence.description: Each file defined its own review checklist with different items (e.g. beginner clarity only in FRONTEND_QUALITY.md, screen reader only in PREMIUM_EXPERIENCE_OS.md).

findings.impact: A milestone could pass one list while failing another.
findings.remediation: DESIGN_REVIEW_GATE.md holds the union as gate authority; the other two point to it.

findings.title: Routing orders disagree

evidence.description: COST_FIRST_ROUTER.md had 6 steps without open source; BUILD_VS_BUY.md asked about open source; the Cycle 0 instruction places open source third.

findings.impact: Inconsistent build-vs-buy outcomes.
findings.remediation: Unified 7-step order with hard filters in COST_FIRST_ROUTER.md; BUILD_VS_BUY.md references it.

findings.title: Review gates outside the gates directory naming scheme

evidence.description: Numbered gates live in gates/G*.md; the two review gates are root files referenced by name in prompts/CLAUDE_CYCLE0_ADDENDUM.md.

findings.impact: Gate discovery inconsistent.
findings.remediation: Registered as gate ids DESIGN_REVIEW and COST_REVIEW in the schema and hierarchy; files left in place to keep references valid. Moving them is optional future cleanup.

findings.title: Superseded update artifacts in repository root

evidence.description: APPLY_THIS_UPDATE.md is a one-time installation note; the zip is 22 bytes and unzip reports it empty.

findings.impact: Confusing, non-authoritative files at root.
findings.remediation: APPLY_THIS_UPDATE.md annotated as applied/superseded. Zip left for owner removal (agent does not delete user-provided files).

findings.title: FILE_INDEX not verified against the tree

evidence.description: No check tied FILE_INDEX.md to actual files.

findings.impact: Index drift.
findings.remediation: Regenerated; npm run check fails on any missing or extra entry.

verification.method: test: FILE_INDEX lists every file and no missing files

findings.title: Unreferenced canonical files and unrepresented platforms

evidence.description: No authority referenced governance/HUMAN_CONTROL.md, app-dev/PLATFORM_MATRIX.md or growth/FULL_FUNNEL.md; the platform matrix lists bots, AI agents, data pipelines, games and IoT companions that no profile field could express; DATA_MODEL.md lacked the new entities.

findings.impact: Requirements silently ignored.
findings.remediation: Added to hierarchy and ADR-014; product types extended; DATA_MODEL.md extended.

findings.title: Repository is not under version control

evidence.description: No .git directory; git 2.53 is installed.

findings.impact: Immutability of findings/ADRs, exact change evidence and CI all depend on version history.
findings.remediation: Owner decision OD-8 (git hosting + CI); recommended before M1.

findings.title: Universal LLM addendum arrived mid-cycle and replaced FILE_INDEX.md

evidence.description: FILE_INDEX.md was overwritten with a 15-entry addendum list (full repository index lost); the accompanying zip is 22 bytes and empty; the 15 listed files are present on disk.

findings.impact: Index no longer described the repository; addendum requirements were not yet in the architecture.
findings.remediation: FILE_INDEX.md regenerated for the full tree; requirements incorporated as ADR-012 Amendment A, ProviderPolicy and LLMConnection schemas, and an extended ModelProvider schema.

verification.method: test: FILE_INDEX lists every file; provider-policy and llm-connection fixtures and mutations pass

findings.title: Undefined term: Project Genome

evidence.description: os/ai/AI_PORTABILITY.md lists "Project Genome" as canonical; no other file defines it.

findings.impact: Agents may invent a new canonical artifact.
findings.remediation: Owner to define or remove the term (OD-11); until then it has no schema or authority.

findings.title: Provider-specific bias in canonical AI runtime wording

evidence.description: ADR-012 listed Anthropic candidates first and the Cycle 0 addendum calls Claude Code first-class, while the Universal LLM addendum forbids canonical workflows requiring a named provider.

findings.impact: Readers could treat one vendor as the canonical engine.
findings.remediation: Amendment A states candidates are non-canonical and Claude Code/Codex are first-class adapters, not privileged engines (strongest-rule principle).
